payload.name: Extract offers from polite closing phrases
payload.description: When a speaker offers help, support, tips, or assistance within a polite closing phrase, use during extraction to create a candidate capturing the offer.
content: During extraction, recognize explicit offers of help, support, tips, or assistance even when they appear in polite closings like 'if you need anything, just let me know'; extract the offer as a memory candidate, including what was offered and to whom.
Do not let the courtesy framing suppress the underlying commitment; an offer is an event or relational fact even if phrased as an afterthought.

solves: The diagnosed cause was an explicit offer of support being omitted during extraction because it was embedded in a polite closing phrase, so the fact never reached memory. Similar omissions occur whenever a speaker offers concrete help, tips, or assistance as a courteous afterthought. This rule applies during extraction to any message containing a clear offer of assistance regardless of topic; it does not apply to vague pleasantries that contain no actual offer.
